components.summary: Public lazy API, CLI dispatch with summary/--json output, and the fuel-cell example
responsibilities: Expose the native API through literal lazy owner exports
Dispatch CLI leaves to qualification, mesh owners; print a short summary by default and the full report with --json
Construct the packaged fuel-cell example without adding domain semantics
side_effects: Read declared CLI inputs; print a summary or the full JSON report

components.summary: Shared contracts, compact reports, clock and finite replay helpers
responsibilities: Derive required Guards from claim semantics and claim assertion kinds and validate shared contract shapes; validate event clocks, homogeneous time kinds and scenario-local event identities; own the shared per-Guard boundary semantics table and derive unmapped semantics only outside selected Guard boundaries; validate event-linked transitions, participant fields and reserved event-time names

Provide pure event and token replay, norm activation and safe scalar scenario evaluation shared by Guards and claim assertions; expose unscoped event times in hours and replay linked token transitions in event order
Keep compact native reports and the conservative four-status aggregation
side_effects: Read declared mapping files (YAML only when PyYAML is installed) and emit JSON only when requested

components.summary: Seven sole native Guard checkers and their finite failure catalog
responsibilities: Run every native declaration and execution rule in one Guard checker; preserve actual failures alongside boundaries; emit one code per problem; detect ambiguous simultaneous events, duplicate unique tokens and missing event participants
Maintain native good cases and protected failure-class oracles without author-supervision proof
side_effects: Return native Guard results; family checks execute finite good and known-bad cases

components.summary: Unit qualification that runs the derived Guards and checks the claim assertions against the model
responsibilities: Run each derived native Guard exactly once
Evaluate each claim.asserts row against the world model; a false row fails the claim, an unresolved row is a gap, and a claim without assertions is not bound (gap)
Expose one row per problem and checked Guard/claim counts with a single final status; check optional entity registries across Guard inputs
Expose the run_worldguard kernel through one qualification owner
side_effects: Execute selected native Guards and return a bounded report

components.summary: Native per-node checks with mesh topology, authority and handoffs
responsibilities: Validate model authority, ports, handoffs, freshness and graph structure
Execute every node contract once; missing contracts gap, false assertions fail, and unbound claims gap the mesh
Preserve every node report and problem under one final status, with checked node and edge counts
state: Immutable node reports and mesh findings
side_effects: Execute declared native mesh nodes and emit in-memory evidence

components.summary: CI on every push and publication of one CI-checked source
responsibilities: Run the test suite, strict FlowGuard map check, release check and skill install check on every push
Check source/version/changelog identity, wait for CI success on the exact SHA, and create the stable tag and Release at that commit
side_effects: CI is read-only; an explicit release commit or manual workflow publishes with GitHub token

components.summary: Portable skill installer and installed-copy check
responsibilities: Install the skill and copy the worldguard package into its runtime directory; check an installed copy
side_effects: install replaces the target skill copy; check and dry-run modes are read-only

components.summary: Portable skill launcher and the references it serves
responsibilities: Run the installed runtime copy when present, otherwise the repository package, without writing bytecode
Keep contract and reporting instructions aligned with the CLI
side_effects: Run only the native WorldGuard CLI
